cli.message: storage locked: <path>
cli.cause: Another process holds the store: a persistent store takes exclusive ownership of its directory and WAL, or its `.rl` file, at open.
cli.remedy: Close the other opener, or open with `--read-only` (a directory store can be read beside its writer; a `.rl` file only while no writer holds it). Not retryable until the other opener exits.
cli.note: The error object's `message` is `storage locked: <path>`; stderr prints `Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`. A `--read-only` open of a `.rl` file is refused the same way while a writer holds it. For a directory store, `<path>` is the writer lock file inside it. `relate serve` on a store another process holds stops at startup with `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>` and exit code 1, not 5 ([cli-serve-open-failed](/docs/reference/errors#cli-serve-open-failed)); `relate clone` of a held `.rl` source exits 1 too ([cli-clone-locked](/docs/reference/errors#cli-clone-locked)).

engine.message: storage locked: <path>
engine.cause: Another process holds the store for writing when a client opens it: `relate.connect(path)` in Python, `Database.open(path)` in Node.js.
engine.remedy: Close the other opener, or open a directory store read-only beside its writer.
engine.note: Python raises `OperationalError` with kind `StorageError` and this message. The Node.js client (@relate/relate 0.16.1) reports every `Database.open` failure, this one, a missing store and a `{ readOnly: true }` open of a `.rl` store a writable handle holds included, as `RelateError` with message `internal error`, code `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, stage `internal` and `gqlStatus` `42000`. The CLI reports the lock as [cli-conflict-locked](/docs/reference/errors#cli-conflict-locked). The Java, Go and Swift clients report the same: `DatabaseException` (Java), `*relate.Error` (Go) or `RelateError.engine` (Swift) with message `internal error`, code `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, GQL status `42000`, stage internal, for a locked store, a second writable open in the same process, and a read-only open of a missing path.
